title: Testing Files
story: Scripts check the world before they act. -f tests for a file and -d for a directory.
goal: For each argument print file, dir or missing depending on what it is.

tests.label: mixed
tests.expect:
a.txt: file
logs: dir
nope: missing

hints: Loop over "$@" and test each with -f and -d.
Use elif for the second test, else for missing.

for p in "$@"; do
  if [ -f "$p" ]; then echo "$p: file"
  elif [ -d "$p" ]; then echo "$p: dir"
  else echo "$p: missing"
  fi
done
socratic: What is the order of the tests and why does it matter?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Testing Files”?
solution:
for p in "$@"; do
  if [ -f "$p" ]; then echo "$p: file"
  elif [ -d "$p" ]; then echo "$p: dir"
  else echo "$p: missing"
  fi
done
